questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution required'.**

The environment is __on threat__ hedgerows and woodlands are vanishing.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 3) i.e. 'under threat'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• The error lies in Part (on threat) of the sentence.
 
• The **structure** of the given sentence is incorrect.
 
• Here in the given sentence, we have to use the preposition **'under'** instead of **'on.'**
 
• **'Use of under'-** is used to mean a lower place or hidden by something; used to talk about lower in age or number; to talk about the state of something.
 
• **'Use of on'-** to denote when a thing is touching the surface of a place; to mark dates and days.
 
• The given sentence makes sense that **the environment is in a state of degradation.**
 
• Therefore, the use of '**on threat**' in the sentence should be replaced with 'under threat' to make it** grammatically correct.**
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Correct sentence:__ *The environment is **__under threat__** hedgerows and woodlands are vanishing.*

questions.question:
**Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'.**

One day __as mine__ little sister said she wanted to become an actress, we were shocked.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 2) i.e. 'when my.'

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• The error lies in Part (as mine) of the sentence.
 
• The structure of the given sentence is incorrect.
 
• The **main clause is “we were shocked”** and the additional information is **“One day my**** little sister said she wanted to become an actress.”**
 
• To join** the two clauses here we have to use 'when,'** which indicates the time of the second event is very close to the time of the first event.
 
• According to rules of grammar,** 'mine' **is used after a** noun** and **'my'** is used before a** noun.**
 
• Here **the noun is 'little sister' **and we have to **use 'my' before it.**
 
• Therefore, the use of 'as mine' in the sentence should be replaced with 'when my' to make it grammatically correct.
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Correct sentence:__ *One day **__when my__** little sister said she wanted to become an actress, we were shocked.*

• **Example:**
 
 
• **​***I saw the room in the Hindu hostel** where** Rajendra Prasad stayed.*
 
 
 
• **When- **it is a **relative pronoun** and it modifies a phrase that expresses time.

• Therefore, the use of 'when' in the sentence should be replaced with 'where' to make it grammatically correct.
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Correct sentence:__ *I recently visited the school __**where**__ I studied in Class 10.*

questions.question:
**The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.**

Please ensure / that you covering your face / with a mask / when you go out.
questions.solution:
The erroneous part is option 1) i.e. 'that you covering your face.'

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• The error lies in the part 'that you covering your face.'
 
• The erroneous part is in **present continuous form (sub+ am/is/are+ verb+ing + object)**
 
• We can note that the **'be verb' is missing after the subject.**
 
• As the **subject here is 'you'** and** the 'be verb' in respect to 'you' is 'are'.**
 
• In the given sentence we need to **add 'are' after 'you'** to make the sentence grammatically correct.
 
• Example:
 
 
• ***Ratan is reading** the history book patiently.*
 
 
 
• Hence, the correct answer is option 1.

 

Correct sentence:__ *Please ensure **that you are covering your face** with a mask when you go out.*

questions.question:

He moved on the undergrowth / quickly and silently, / hiding / from the enemy.
questions.solution:
The erroneous part is option 2) i.e. 'He moved on the undergrowth.'

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• The error lies in part 'He moved on the undergrowth.'
 
• In the erroneous part, the use of the preposition is wrong.
 
• **'On' **is used to denote when a thing is touching the surface of a place; to indicate dates and days.
 
• But in the given sentence, the subject is moving into the undergrowth in order to hide from the view of the enemy.
 
• The correct preposition should be **'into.'**
 
• **'Into' **is used to denote when something is within or inside something else.
 
• Example:
 
 
• *He put the important documents **into** a special folder.*
 
 
 
• *​*Therefore we need to **replace 'on' with 'into'** to make the sentence grammatically correct.
 
• Hence, the correct answer is option 2.

 

Correct sentence:__ ***He moved into the undergrowth** quickly and silently, hiding from the enemy.*
